title: Fini AI vs Agentforce: Which Salesforce AI Wins?
summary: Compare Agentforce and Fini on pricing, deployment, knowledge maintenance, resolution tracking, and compliance for AI customer support.
body_markdown:
Support leaders comparing these two are usually asked to answer a product question. The question in front of them is closer to an architecture question. Fini is a per-resolution AI agent backed by Y Combinator and Matrix Partners that runs on top of the helpdesk you already have. Salesforce Agentforce is the agent layer of the Salesforce platform, priced on consumption, and since July 2026 also available as Agentforce Help Agent on a pay-per-resolution basis.


## One question decides this, and it is not about the AI


Both of these resolve tickets well. Neither of them is a weak product, and a feature grid will not separate them, because the features converge every quarter.


What separates them is what each one has to be standing on before it resolves anything. That splits into three questions, and they are the spine of this comparison:


1.


**Is Salesforce your system of record?** Everything downstream follows from this one answer.


2.


**How many meters end up on the invoice?** Both publish rates. They do not publish the same number of them.


3.


**Who owns the knowledge after go-live?** This is where the running cost actually lives.


Work those three in order and the decision usually makes itself, well before anyone opens a checklist.

## What is Fini?


Fini is an AI agent for customer support that resolves tickets end to end across chat, email, and voice in 130+ languages. It publishes a 90%[resolution rate](https://www.usefini.com/glossary/resolution-rate) at 99% accuracy and runs more than 3 million resolutions a month across fintech and healthcare teams. Pricing is a single plan price with a monthly allowance of resolved tickets and no per-seat fees. Fini connects by one-click OAuth to the helpdesk you already run, Zendesk, Intercom, HubSpot, Front, Freshdesk, Livechat, Gorgias, Slack, and Salesforce among them, takes actions inside your billing and records systems, and writes the decision audit trail back.


## What is Salesforce Agentforce?


Agentforce is the[agentic AI](https://www.usefini.com/glossary/agentic-ai) layer of the Salesforce platform. Salesforce announced general availability of Agentforce 360 on 13 October 2025 at Dreamforce, bringing the Agentforce platform, Data 360, the Customer 360 apps, and Slack into one system, with Agentforce Builder for building agents conversationally, Agent Script for tighter control of agent behaviour, Agentforce Voice, and Intelligent Context for grounding agents in unstructured data. Underneath sits a reasoning engine Salesforce calls Atlas, which breaks a request into steps and plans across them, and the Salesforce Trust Layer, which handles secure grounding, data masking, toxicity detection, and a zero data retention policy at the third-party model layer.


In July 2026 Salesforce shipped Agentforce Help Agent, a purpose-built customer support agent with prepackaged actions, channel setup for voice, web, portal, and messaging from a single screen, and pay-per-resolution pricing. Salesforce runs the same technology on its own help site, where it reports 4.3 million inquiries handled and 70% resolved. Salesforce is also mid-transaction on the AI support vendor formerly known as Intercom, having signed a definitive agreement on 15 June 2026 with close expected in its fiscal fourth quarter of 2027, so the shape of its support portfolio is still moving.


This is a serious product from the largest vendor in the category, and the honest version of this comparison says so early.


## What the agent is standing on


Read one clause from Salesforce's own Help Agent launch and the whole decision comes into focus. The agent, Salesforce writes, is grounded on your Salesforce Knowledge.


That is a reasonable design. It is also a dependency, and it is worth following the chain all the way down before signing anything.


Salesforce Knowledge is a Service Cloud module. On Salesforce's published Service Cloud pricing, Knowledge Management appears as read-only across the editions, with read and write access listed as an additional $75 per user per month. So the knowledge the agent is grounded on is a licensed module, and the ability of your team to write into it is its own line item.


Below that sits the data. Salesforce grounds agent context in Data 360, and the credit examples on its own pricing page carry a note that they exclude Data 360 credits and other consumption services. Below that sits the deployment surface, the Agentforce Customer Service Portal, which is the channel Salesforce names as the common home for Help Agent. And beside all of it sits the action layer: out of the box the agent answers questions and manages cases, while order management, appointment scheduling, and account management are added through Agentforce Builder or, in Salesforce's own words, the coding agent of the customer's choosing.


None of that is hidden. Salesforce publishes every piece of it, which is more than most vendors in this category do. The point is not that the list is long. The point is what the list assumes: that Salesforce is already the system of record, the knowledge base, the data layer, the portal, and the[orchestration](https://www.usefini.com/glossary/ai-agent-orchestration) surface. For a company where all five are already true, the agent is close to free to stand up, and Agentforce is very likely the right answer. For a company where none of them are true, the AI decision has quietly become a platform decision.


Fini answers the same question with one line. It stands on the helpdesk you already run. Connecting it is one-click OAuth with no engineering on your side, Salesforce included, so a team running Service Cloud can evaluate Fini against live Salesforce tickets without moving a case, a queue, or a routing rule. That is the actual difference between the two, and everything below is downstream of it.

### How much does Agentforce cost per conversation?


A standard action costs 20 Flex Credits, and at $500 per 100,000 credits that is $0.10 per action. The number nobody publishes is how many actions one conversation consumes. A support conversation that looks up an order, checks a policy and updates a record is three actions before it answers anything, so $0.10 per action is not comparable to a $0.99 or $0.49 per-resolution rate. The 2.5M annual credit allowance works out at roughly 125,000 standard actions per org per year. Before signing, ask Salesforce for the average action count per resolved conversation on accounts like yours, in writing.

The arithmetic is worth doing with Salesforce's own examples rather than anyone else's. Salesforce prices Flex Credits at $500 per 100,000, which puts a credit at half a cent and a standard action at $0.10. Its published self-service example, a customer asking where their order is, uses two actions, so 40 credits, so $0.20 per request. Its case management example uses three actions at $0.30, and it scales that to 100 users handling three cases a day for 20 days at $1,800 a month. The 2.5M annual credit allowance on an Agentforce 1 edition works out at roughly 10,400 standard actions a month, or about 5,200 customer requests at Salesforce's own two-action rate.


Set that beside the outcome-priced options and the comparison sharpens. Help Agent bills $2 per autonomous resolution and charges nothing when a customer escalates or leaves unhappy. Fini's plan price divided by its full allowance is $1.80 per resolution on Growth and $1.13 on Scale, and that figure covers the platform, implementation, and every escalation. Those are the two numbers to put side by side, because they are the only two that include everything.


Annual billing takes 17% off the Fini price. Enterprise adds a 90-day pilot on live traffic with resolution, CSAT, and accuracy targets agreed in writing, all backed by the[Zero Pay Guarantee](https://www.usefini.com/blog/the-fini-zero-pay-guarantee-ai-that-delivers-or-you-pay-nothing) : miss the agreed resolution target and the fees are waived.


## How Fini and Agentforce differ


Three differences move deals. Each is worth checking against your own ticket data rather than a feature list.


### 1. What the invoice counts


Fini bills when the issue is solved with no human involved, and escalations to your team are free. One meter, one definition, published on the pricing page.


Salesforce now offers a definition that is just as clean, and a page that claimed otherwise would be out of date. On Help Agent pay-per-resolution, you are charged when the agent resolves an issue autonomously from start to finish, and if the customer gives negative feedback or asks for a human there is no charge. Salesforce also states that Data 360 and Agentforce are unmetered during the agent interaction, which removes the forecasting problem that consumption pricing usually creates.


The difference is not the definition. It is how many meters sit around it. Fini's plan price is the entire bill. The outcome rate on Help Agent sits alongside Service Cloud seats, and next to any employee-facing agent add-on, knowledge write access, and Data 360 consumption a given org happens to need. Both invoices are forecastable. Only one of them is forecastable from two numbers you already have.


### 2. Who owns the knowledge after go-live


This is the difference that compounds, and it is covered in depth in the feature comparison below. In short: Fini's knowledge layer writes and reconciles itself from resolved tickets, while Agentforce is grounded on a knowledge base your team writes and maintains, with write access licensed separately.


### 3. How fast each goes live


Fini goes live on a staged 30-day path. Day 1 connects the helpdesk and knowledge base and the agent begins answering in shadow mode. Day 14 it handles live traffic on the journeys that clear the confidence threshold, and agentic workflows are running. Day 30 it runs autonomously on the agreed scope with escalation rules in place. On Enterprise that sits inside a 90-day pilot on live traffic with targets agreed in writing before anything is billed.


Agentforce has two answers now, and both are true. Help Agent is designed to stand up quickly, with prepackaged actions, drag-and-drop file or URL grounding, a preview pane for testing, and channels enabled from one screen. That is a real change from a year ago. A configured multi-agent programme is a different exercise: Salesforce does not publish a timeline for it, and third-party implementation practices describe first agents in the region of six to sixteen weeks and larger programmes running longer, usually with a partner and usually gated on data readiness rather than on the agent itself.


The honest read is that the gap has narrowed at the simple end and remains at the complex end. If your first use case is deflecting help-centre questions, both are fast. If it involves reaching into a ledger, a claims system, or a core banking platform, ask both vendors who does that integration work and whose invoice it lands on.


## Feature by feature


Beyond the commercial picture, three capabilities separate the two platforms under the hood: how each reasons over your data, how each keeps its knowledge current, and how each proves what it did.


### Architecture and reasoning


**Fini.** Fini runs what it calls[structured execution rather than retrieval-augmented generation](https://www.usefini.com/blog/rag-vs-structured-execution-ai-customer-support) . Instead of retrieving policy text and letting a model paraphrase it, Fini turns policies into executable functions, pulls live account data, and calls backend APIs so an action is confirmed rather than described. The model handles intent recognition and[natural language generation](https://www.usefini.com/glossary/natural-language-generation) , not the policy decision or the calculation. On Fini's published benchmark across 500 real fintech tickets, policy-dependent accuracy rose from about 72% under retrieval to over 98% under structured execution.


**Agentforce.** Salesforce's reasoning engine decomposes a request into steps and plans across them, with hybrid reasoning that lets teams pin deterministic behaviour where they need it and Agent Script for explicit control of how the agent behaves. Grounding runs through the Trust Layer with secure data retrieval against Salesforce records. It is a strong design, and the control surface is deeper than anything a newer vendor ships. Salesforce publishes no retrieval-versus-execution accuracy benchmark of the kind Fini publishes.


**Verdict:** Fini ✓ publishes a structured-execution benchmark and a confirmed-action design. Agentforce ✓ ships deeper authoring control through Agent Script and hybrid reasoning, but ✗ publishes no comparable accuracy benchmark.


### Knowledge management


This is where the two diverge most, and where the running cost of an AI agent actually sits. Every deployment degrades the same way: the help centre drifts, articles start contradicting each other, confidence drops, and the team quietly becomes a documentation factory.


**Fini.** Fini's[Knowledge Atlas](https://www.usefini.com/blog/fini-knowledge-atlas) is a self-maintaining knowledge layer, shipped and generally available. When a human resolves an escalation, it extracts the solution, writes a formatted help article, files it in the right branch of a category tree, and makes it searchable immediately. It flags duplicates, contradictory instructions, and outdated policies on a reconciliation dashboard. It routes by intent rather than keyword, so "why won't my payment go through", "transaction failed at checkout" and "card not working" all reach the same article. And because the knowledge layer is tree-structured rather than a[knowledge graph](https://www.usefini.com/glossary/knowledge-graph) spanning many sources, every answer traces back to exactly one authoritative article rather than a blend of several. Fini reports AI resolution moving from 50-60% to 85-90% and knowledge upkeep falling from about 20 hours a week to two.


**Agentforce.** Agentforce is grounded on Salesforce Knowledge, with Intelligent Context extending grounding into unstructured data and Help Agent adding drag-and-drop files and URL crawling to get a first agent standing without a mature help centre. The connective tissue is good. What Salesforce does not claim is that the platform writes and files the articles for you, and on the Service Cloud price list the ability to write into Knowledge at all is an additional $75 per user per month. Salesforce publishes no before-and-after numbers for knowledge upkeep.


**Verdict:** Fini ✓ self-maintaining knowledge, generally available, with auto-written articles, conflict detection, and single-source attribution, plus published upkeep numbers. Agentforce ✓ broad, well-governed grounding including unstructured data, but ✗ the knowledge itself stays your team's job, and write access is licensed separately.


### Attribution and the audit trail


**Fini.** Because the knowledge layer is tree-structured, a Fini answer resolves to one source article, which is the difference between an auditable answer and a plausible one. As Fini's co-founder Deepak Singla puts it, "most AI tools blend information from multiple articles, creating answers that don't match any single source. That's a compliance violation waiting to happen." Fini scores every answer for confidence and checks it against policy before it sends, escalates anything below the threshold to a human with full context attached, and commits the decision to an audit log. Enterprise adds a full decision audit trail alongside data residency options and BAA and DPA terms.


**Agentforce.** The Trust Layer is Salesforce's answer and it is a substantial one: secure data retrieval that respects existing permissions, dynamic grounding, data masking of personally identifiable information before prompts reach the model, toxicity detection, and a zero data retention policy under which prompts and responses are never stored or used to train the third-party models. Fini states the same on its own pricing page, that customer data is never used to train foundation models, so this is a bar both clear rather than a gap. The open question for a regulated buyer is attribution: when grounding draws across Salesforce Knowledge, Data 360, and crawled sources at once, Salesforce publishes no guarantee that a given answer traces to a single authoritative record.


**Verdict:** Fini ✓ single-source attribution by design, confidence scoring with policy checks before send, and a decision audit trail on Enterprise. Agentforce ✓ a mature, documented trust architecture with permission-aware retrieval and zero data retention, but ✗ publishes no single-source attribution guarantee across blended grounding.


## What Fini customers report


Peaksware builds training software under two brands, TrainingPeaks for endurance athletes and Train Heroic for strength coaching, and that is exactly what made it a hard deployment. The two brands share vocabulary but not policy, so generic AI tools kept answering a question about one with a rule that belonged to the other. Support also runs on a season: volume climbs from Black Friday through February, and at peak, response times had stretched to 24 hours.


> "Our system is so nuanced. There are times where the way someone phrases something may seem like it's a coach when it's an athlete."
>
>
> Kristina Green, Senior Support Rep, TrainingPeaks


That is the attribution problem described by the person who lives with it. An answer assembled from whichever article scored highest is wrong here even when every sentence in it is true somewhere.


Rollout ran in four phases: prompts and guardrails, a knowledge base overhaul with dashboard access, shadow testing in internal comment mode, then iteration and launch on a weekly cadence. At peak, Fini now deflects around 1,200 tickets a week on TrainingPeaks alone and more than 10,000 across the January and February surge, cutting the visible queue by over 70%. Average response time fell to 25.9 seconds and CSAT rose 12%. On Train Heroic the Monday queue dropped from 200-250 tickets to 100-120, a backlog that used to take the whole week now clears by Wednesday, and the team recovered two full days of capacity every week.


The knowledge loop is the part that matters most for this comparison, because it is the thing a support rep has to live with long after go-live.


> "I was able to go in and add a knowledge item very easily and improve the response. That was a huge shift in progressing Fini forward."
>
>
> Darren Lacy, Senior Support Rep, Train Heroic


That sits inside more than 3 million resolutions Fini runs every month at a published 99% accuracy rate, across[fintech and regulated support teams](https://www.usefini.com/blog/how-to-use-ai-agents-for-support-in-fintech) .

## Where Agentforce is stronger


Salesforce is the largest vendor in this category for good reasons, and a comparison that pretends otherwise is not useful to a buyer.


1.


**One platform, one contract.** If Salesforce is already your system of record, the agent inherits your data model, your permissions, your reporting, and your procurement relationship on day one.


2.


**Compliance breadth.** Salesforce's compliance documentation covers SOC 2 and SOC 3, ISO 27001, 27017, 27018, and 42001, HIPAA, HITRUST, FedRAMP, PCI DSS, CSA STAR, and regional attestations. That list is broader than Fini's, and for public-sector buyers FedRAMP can decide the deal outright.


3.


**Control surface.** Agent Script, hybrid reasoning, and Agentforce Builder give an operations team more explicit control over agent behaviour than a threshold-and-policy model does.


4.


**Scope beyond support.** Sales, field service, marketing, and employee-facing agents run on the same platform, which matters if the mandate is company-wide rather than support-only.

On the certifications most commercial buyers gate on, both clear the bar: Fini's[SOC 2 Type II](https://www.usefini.com/glossary/soc-2-type-ii) and[HIPAA-compliant](https://www.usefini.com/glossary/hipaa-compliance) , BAA-eligible handling come with the plan.


## Where Fini is stronger


1.


**It does not require adopting a platform.** Fini runs on top of the helpdesk you already have, Salesforce included, so the AI layer can be evaluated and changed without a platform decision attached to it.


2.


**Knowledge that maintains itself.** Articles written from resolved tickets, conflicts reconciled, every answer traced to one source, with published upkeep numbers behind it.


3.


**One meter.** A plan price that covers platform, implementation, and allowance, so the invoice can be modelled from your ticket volume before a sales call, with no per-seat fees and free escalations.


4.


**A 30-day path to autonomy.** Day 1, Day 14, Day 30, with a 90-day Enterprise pilot on live traffic before anything is billed.


5.


**Built for regulated support.** Confidence scoring with policy checks before send, low-confidence escalation with full context, and a decision audit trail, shipped as the default rather than assembled.


## Which should you choose?


### Choose Fini if you want:


-


To change your AI layer without making a platform decision, whether or not you run Salesforce


-


Knowledge that maintains itself rather than a documentation backlog that grows with ticket volume


-


One published plan price covering platform, implementation, and allowance, with escalations free


-


Single-source attribution and a decision audit trail for regulated review


-


A staged 30-day path to autonomy with targets agreed in writing before billing starts


### Choose Salesforce Agentforce if you want:


-


Salesforce as your system of record, with the agent inheriting that data model and those permissions


-


FedRAMP, HITRUST, PCI DSS, or the wider ISO set as a procurement requirement


-


Deterministic, scripted control over agent behaviour owned by an in-house operations team


-


Agents across sales, service, field service, and employees on one platform and one contract
